removeAppNames: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)

answers.value: All commercial-lines accounts due to renew in the current renewal quarter within the underwriter's assigned book; each account's expiring policy, prior-year premium, incurred losses and loss development are assessed one account at a time.

Prior-three-policy-terms plus the current in-force term (e.g. 2023-2025 policy years) evaluated 90 days ahead of each account's effective date, consistent with the Renewal Review 90 Days Out standard.

Each account record carries expiring premium, incurred + paid losses, IBNR/case reserves, claim count and large-loss flags; a record missing a valued loss run within 60 days of the review date is returned to the Underwriting Assistant for a refreshed extract before assessment.

Account count on the assessment worksheet reconciles to the renewal book listing from PolicyCenter (delta = 0); summed expiring premium ties to the in-force premium bordereau within a 1% tolerance, breaks investigated.

The prior-year performance summary is saved to the underwriting file in OpenText under /UW/Renewals/<policy-number>/ with the loss-valuation date and version label, retained per the record-retention schedule (7 years).

Accounts with adverse development or a loss ratio above the line-of-business target are logged on the referral tracker with disposition (re-rate / restructure / refer to Senior Underwriter) and the reason recorded.
Loss-development factors and trend selections follow the approved renewal-analysis methodology v3 issued by Pricing/Actuarial; the LDF pattern version is recorded on the worksheet.
Sensitivity checked by re-running loss development at the low/central/high LDF selection; a swing greater than 5 points in the projected loss ratio triggers a note and Senior Underwriter review.
Accounts with expiring premium over $250k, or projected loss ratio over the LOB target, are treated as material and individually documented rather than assessed on a portfolio basis.
A 5% monthly sample of assessed renewal accounts, plus 100% of accounts with expiring premium over $250k, pulled for the Underwriting Quality review.

PASS = loss data valued within 60 days, loss ratio computed against the correct LOB target, and adverse accounts flagged for action; FAIL = stale loss data, wrong target applied, or an adverse account not flagged.
Failed samples are returned to the underwriter for re-work within 5 business days; repeat findings are escalated to the Underwriting Director / Manager and captured in the QA log.
Acceptance = every in-scope renewal account has a documented prior-year performance summary with a valued loss ratio and a retain/re-rate/exit recommendation before the strategy is set.
Evidence located in OpenText /UW/Renewals/<policy-number>/ and summarised in the renewal book workbook stored in the underwriting workstation.

Field definitions come from the PolicyCenter renewal-data dictionary (expiring_premium, incurred_loss, paid_loss, case_reserve, claim_count); control total = book count and expiring premium reconciled to the in-force bordereau at extract time.

checklist.step: Start the prior-year assessment at least 90 days before the renewal effective date
checklist.value: Renewal review is triggered from the PolicyCenter renewal diary 90 days out; the assessment date is stamped on the account worksheet.

checklist.step: Pull a valued loss run for each account under review
checklist.value: Loss runs valued within 60 days of the review date are attached to every account before performance is judged.

testing.step: Verify review timing across the book
testing.value: For a sample of renewed accounts, the documented assessment date is >=90 days before effective date; 0 late starts without a logged exception.

checklist.step: Compare each account's loss ratio to the line-of-business target
checklist.value: Projected loss ratio computed and compared to the current LOB loss-ratio target on the worksheet; variance highlighted.

testing.value: Sampled accounts use the target for the correct LOB and term; 0 mismatches between account LOB and applied target.

checklist.step: Record the performance conclusion in the underwriting file
checklist.value: Prior-year performance summary and retain/re-rate/exit recommendation filed to OpenText /UW/Renewals/<policy-number>/.

testing.value: 100% of assessed accounts have a filed performance summary with a valued loss ratio; missing files reopened.

answers.value: Every account in the underwriter's renewal book for the quarter, each assigned exactly one tier: retain (on-strategy, profitable), re-rate (needs rate/terms correction) or exit (outside appetite or unprofitable).
The current renewal quarter, tiered 90 days ahead of each account's effective date so exit and re-rate decisions leave time for state-required non-renewal notice.

Each account carries prior-year loss ratio, appetite fit, rate-adequacy indication and retention priority; an account cannot be tiered until the prior-year performance assessment is complete and the appetite/no-write check is run.
Sum of retain + re-rate + exit counts equals total book count (delta = 0); every account has exactly one tier, and tiered premium reconciles to the in-force premium listing within 1%.
The tiered book listing is saved as a versioned workbook in the underwriting workstation and the tier plus rationale is written to each account's file in OpenText, dated and version-labelled.
Exit-tier accounts are logged with the no-write / appetite reason and routed for non-renewal handling; borderline accounts are logged for Senior Underwriter adjudication with disposition recorded.
Tiering rules follow the approved renewal-segmentation methodology v3 (loss-ratio bands, appetite matrix, rate-need thresholds); the ruleset version is recorded on the listing.
Boundary sensitivity documented: accounts within 5 points of a tier threshold are re-checked and, if still borderline, escalated rather than auto-tiered.
Accounts with expiring premium over $250k or in the exit tier are treated as material and individually justified in the file.
5% monthly sample of tiered accounts plus 100% of exit-tier and over-$250k accounts, traced back to the PolicyCenter source data.

PASS = tier matches the documented rule given the account's loss ratio and appetite fit, with a rationale on file; FAIL = tier inconsistent with the rule, missing rationale, or exit account with no non-renewal action.
Mis-tiered accounts are corrected and re-filed within 5 business days; systemic mis-tiering is escalated to the Underwriting Director / Manager.
Acceptance = 100% of book accounts carry exactly one tier with a documented rationale, and exit accounts have a non-renewal path opened in time for state notice periods.
Evidence located in the tiered book workbook in the underwriting workstation and each account's OpenText renewal folder.

Approved methodology = renewal-segmentation ruleset v3; parameters (loss-ratio bands, appetite matrix, rate-need thresholds) sourced from the current Pricing/Underwriting appetite guide and recorded on the listing header.

checklist.step: Tier accounts against segment retention targets
checklist.value: Retain/re-rate/exit tiers are set so the retained book supports the retention-rate target for each segment; segment target shown on the listing.

testing.value: Projected retained premium by segment reconciles to the retention plan; deviations over 5 points flagged to Senior Underwriter.

checklist.step: Screen each account against documented appetite
checklist.value: Every account checked against the appetite matrix (LOB, geography, industry); out-of-appetite accounts routed to the exit tier.

testing.value: 0 accounts tiered retain that fall outside documented appetite without a documented CUO exception.

checklist.step: Run the no-write list against the book
checklist.value: Book cross-checked to the enforced no-write list; any match is tiered exit and flagged for non-renewal.

testing.value: 0 no-write accounts tiered retain or re-rate; matches evidenced on the tiering worksheet.

answers.value: The producing broker or agent for each renewing account, with early engagement for strategic accounts (expiring premium over $250k or key-relationship flag); communication covers the intended rate action, terms changes and any non-renewal.
Renewal strategy conveyed no later than 60 days before effective date (Quote to Broker 60 Days Out), with strategic-account outreach beginning at the 90-day review.
Each renewal communication records the account, producer, intended rate/terms, message date and channel; a communication cannot be marked sent without a linked account tier and an approved strategy.
Count of communications logged reconciles to the count of renewing accounts requiring producer contact (delta = 0); strategic accounts show an outreach date on or before the 90-day mark.
The renewal-strategy note and outbound message are saved to the account file in OpenText and the broker portal thread, dated and version-labelled; email confirmations attached.
Accounts where the broker disputes the strategy are logged with disposition (negotiate / hold / escalate to Senior Underwriter); non-renewals are logged to ensure no silent non-renewal occurs.
Messaging follows the approved renewal-communication playbook v3 and the account's approved renewal strategy; the strategy version referenced is noted on the communication record.
For strategic accounts a talking-point pack covering best/expected/worst renewal outcomes is prepared so the underwriter can hold the rate position under pushback.
Strategic accounts (over $250k or key relationship) require documented Senior Underwriter sign-off on the message before it is sent; routine accounts follow the standard template.
The renewal decision and rate/terms position communicated are documented in the account file with date and author, and cross-linked to the approved strategy.
Recipients recorded: producing broker/agent name and agency code, plus internal cc (Senior Underwriter for strategic accounts); captured in the broker portal thread.
5% monthly sample of renewal communications plus 100% of strategic accounts, traced through the PolicyCenter/portal workflow history.

PASS = communication sent at least 60 days out, matches the approved strategy, and (for strategic accounts) carries Senior Underwriter approval; FAIL = late, off-strategy, missing approval, or a silent non-renewal.
Late or missing communications are escalated to the Underwriting Director / Manager and remediated within 5 business days; silent non-renewals are treated as a compliance breach and logged.
The delegation matrix in the authority guide governs who may commit a renewal position by premium band and LOB; strategic-account messaging requires Senior Underwriter authority per that matrix.

Approved methodology = renewal-communication playbook v3; parameters (timing thresholds, strategic-account definition, approval bands) sourced from the underwriting authority guide and recorded on the communication log.

answers.value: The renewal pricing strategy for the underwriter's book: segment-level rate direction and guardrails (target rate change by segment, minimum-premium floors, deviation limits) applied across all renewing accounts in the plan year.
The upcoming plan/renewal year, set before the renewal cycle opens and refreshed at mid-year against emerging loss and rate-adequacy indications.

Strategy inputs include actuarial rate indications, prior-year loss ratios by segment, filed-rate levels and retention targets; a strategy cannot be finalised until actuarial indications and the current filed rates are attached.
Target rate changes by segment reconcile to the actuarial indication file and to the portfolio premium base; the weighted average target ties to the plan rate-change assumption within 1 point.
The approved renewal pricing strategy is stored as a versioned document in SharePoint/underwriting workstation and referenced in Earnix pricing configuration, dated and version-labelled.
Segments where the strategy departs from the actuarial indication are logged with rationale and require Pricing Actuary and Senior Underwriter concurrence before adoption.
Pricing strategy uses the approved rate-indication methodology and current filed rate manuals; the actuarial indication version and manual effective date are recorded.
Strategy stress-tested at indicated, plan and conservative rate scenarios; a projected loss-ratio swing over 3 points across scenarios is documented and reviewed with the Pricing Actuary.
Segments contributing over 10% of book premium, or where the target deviates from the indication by more than 5 points, are treated as material and individually justified.
All defined pricing segments in the strategy (census), plus a trace of each segment target back to its actuarial indication source.

PASS = every segment target is within filed-rate authority and supported by an actuarial indication with documented rationale for any deviation; FAIL = target outside filed rates, no indication support, or missing sign-off.
Segments failing review are re-set with the Pricing Actuary before the strategy is published; unresolved items escalate to the Head of Pricing.
Acceptance = a signed-off renewal pricing strategy exists for every segment, tied to actuarial indications and within filed-rate authority, before renewals are re-rated.
Evidence located in the renewal pricing strategy document (SharePoint/underwriting workstation) and the Earnix pricing configuration change record.

Approved methodology = current rate-indication methodology; parameters (segment indications, filed-rate levels, retention/loss-ratio targets) sourced from the Pricing/Actuarial indication file and filed rate manuals, versions recorded on the strategy header.

checklist.step: Anchor segment targets to filed rates
checklist.value: Every segment rate target sits within the filed rate level or an approved deviation band; filed-rate reference recorded.

testing.value: 0 segment targets exceed filed-rate authority without a documented, approved deviation.

testing.value: Renewals price through Earnix using the strategy configuration; 0 material accounts priced outside the tool.

checklist.step: Set targets to meet LOB loss-ratio goals
checklist.value: Segment rate direction is chosen so the projected book loss ratio meets the LOB target; projection attached to the strategy.

testing.value: Projected loss ratio under the strategy meets or beats the LOB target, or the gap is documented and approved.

All policies with effective dates in the forward 4-month window (current renewal quarter plus the next month for lead time); regenerated at the start of each cycle.
Each listing row carries policy number, insured, LOB, expiring premium, effective date and assigned underwriter; rows missing effective date or expiring premium are rejected and the extract re-run.
Row count and total expiring premium on the listing reconcile to the PolicyCenter in-force report for the same window (delta = 0 on count, within 1% on premium); breaks investigated before release.

Premium-band boundaries are documented; accounts within 5% of a band boundary are checked so they are not mis-banded.
The over-$250k and strategic-priority segments are treated as material and reconciled individually to the in-force report.
100% of policies in the extract window (census); the automated extract is validated end to end against the SOR.

answers.value: Renewal accounts whose strategy exceeds the underwriter's authority and require Senior Underwriter or Underwriting Director/Manager approval: those breaching premium/limit authority, exceeding the deviation band, or in the exit tier.
The current renewal quarter, flagged at the 90-day review so approvals are secured before quotes are released to producers.

Flagged-account count reconciles to the referral triggers applied against the book (delta = 0); every account over the authority thresholds appears on the approval list.
The approval-required list is saved to the underwriting workstation and each account file in OpenText records the referral with date and version; the referral queue is tracked in Power BI.
Accounts pending approval are logged with disposition (approved / declined / conditions); accounts released without approval are treated as authority breaches and escalated.
Referral triggers follow the approved underwriting authority matrix v3.2 (premium, limit, LOB, deviation thresholds); the matrix version is recorded on the flagging worksheet.
Accounts within 10% of an authority threshold are re-checked so borderline cases are referred rather than retained in-authority.
All exit-tier accounts and accounts over $250k are treated as material and individually confirmed against the authority matrix.
5% monthly sample of renewal accounts plus 100% of accounts over authority thresholds, checked for correct flagging and referral.
PASS = every account exceeding authority is flagged with the correct approval level and a recommendation; FAIL = an over-authority account not flagged, wrong level assigned, or no recommendation.
Missed referrals are corrected before quote release; an account bound over authority without approval is escalated to the Underwriting Director / Manager and logged as an authority breach.
Acceptance = 100% of over-authority and exit-tier accounts appear on the approval list with the correct approval level before any quote is issued.
Evidence located in the approval-required worksheet in the underwriting workstation and the referral note in each OpenText account file.

testing.value: 0 accounts meeting a referral trigger left off the approval list.

checklist.value: Each account's premium, limit and LOB are compared to the authority matrix to determine the required approver.

testing.value: Sampled flagged accounts map to the correct approval level per the matrix; 0 mis-levelled referrals.

checklist.step: Route referrals with a recommendation

answers.value: The underwriter's renewal book tracked through the cycle for retention rate and premium change (rate + exposure) against the renewal plan, monitored at book and segment level.
The full renewal cycle to date (cycle inception through current), refreshed at least weekly and reviewed monthly against plan.
Tracking captures policies offered, renewed, lost and pending, plus renewal premium vs expiring; a period is invalid until offered/renewed/lost counts reconcile to PolicyCenter transaction status.
Renewed + lost + pending equals total policies up for renewal in the period (delta = 0); renewal premium change ties to the billed premium movement in PolicyCenter within 1%.
Each monitoring snapshot is retained in the renewal Power BI dashboard and exported to the underwriting workstation with the as-of date and version for the monthly review pack.
Segments tracking below retention target or off the rate-change plan are logged with disposition (corrective action / accept / escalate) and reviewed with the Senior Underwriter.

Retention and rate-change metrics use the approved renewal-KPI definition v3 (retention = renewed premium / available premium; rate change per the pricing methodology); definition version recorded on the dashboard.
Retention measured on both policy-count and premium bases; a divergence over 5 points between the two prompts investigation of large-account movement.
Segments over 10% of book premium, and any single account over $250k lost, are treated as material and called out individually in the monitoring pack.
All renewal transactions in the cycle-to-date (census for the KPI), with a 5% sample re-computed by hand to validate the dashboard.
PASS = dashboard retention and rate-change figures reconcile to PolicyCenter and match the KPI definition; FAIL = reconciliation break, wrong KPI formula, or stale (>7 days) data.
Data or formula errors are corrected and the dashboard re-published; segments off-plan are escalated to the Senior Underwriter / Portfolio UW Manager for corrective action.
Acceptance = retention and premium-change are tracked and reconciled at least weekly, with segments off target flagged and a monthly review pack produced.
Evidence located in the renewal Power BI workspace and the monthly monitoring pack in the underwriting workstation.
In-scope period = cycle inception to current as-of date; effective dates covered are the renewals falling in the current cycle, refreshed weekly.
Approved methodology = renewal-KPI definition v3; parameters (retention formula, rate-change basis, segment targets) sourced from the renewal plan and stamped on the dashboard.

Field definitions from the PolicyCenter renewal-transaction dictionary (policy status, renewed_premium, expiring_premium, rate_change); control total = transaction counts and premium reconciled to the in-force/billed reports at each refresh.

checklist.value: Retention and premium-change are monitored on a recurring (>=weekly) cadence, not just at cycle end.

answers.value: Each renewing account being re-rated: the current filed rate level is applied to the account's renewal exposure base (updated payroll/sales/units/values) to calculate the rated renewal premium.

5% monthly sample of renewal accounts with coverage changes plus 100% of accounts adding exclusions or restricting coverage, traced to the issued forms in PolicyCenter.

PASS = each coverage change is supported by a documented risk-quality driver, uses a current filed form, and is issued as decided; FAIL = change without a documented driver, non-filed form used without approval, or a decided change not issued.

Discrepancies between decided and issued coverage are corrected before renewal issuance; manuscript-wording needs are escalated to the Wordings Coverage Specialist and, if outside filed forms, to Compliance.
Acceptance = every coverage/exclusion/deductible change is documented with its risk driver, uses filed forms (or approved manuscript wording), and matches the issued endorsements.
Evidence located in the coverage-decision note in OpenText and the endorsement/forms record in the PolicyCenter policy transaction.

answers.value: Each renewed or re-rated account: the renewal analysis rationale and rate-change justification are documented in the underwriting file, covering loss performance, exposure changes, rate action and any deviations.
The renewal term, documented at the point of quote/bind decision and finalised before the effective date for each account in the cycle.
The file note must state loss ratio, rate change, exposure change, deviations and approvals; a renewal cannot be marked complete until the rationale note and required sign-offs are present.
Count of bound renewals reconciles to the count of filed rationale notes (delta = 0); every deviation flagged during rating has a matching justification in the file.
The rationale note is stored in the account file in OpenText under /UW/Renewals/<policy-number>/ with author, date and version, and linked from the PolicyCenter policy record; retained 7 years.
Files missing a rationale or a required approval are logged as documentation exceptions with disposition and remediated; repeat gaps are escalated to the Underwriting Director / Manager.
Documentation follows the approved renewal file-documentation standard v3 (required elements checklist); the standard version is referenced in the file template.
Not a modelled calculation; documentation depth scales with account size — files over $250k require a fuller rationale and, where deviations exist, the supporting analysis is attached.
Accounts over $250k and any account with a rate deviation are treated as material and require a complete, individually reviewed rationale on file.
Monthly 5% sample of bound renewals plus 100% of over-$250k and deviation accounts, inspected for a complete rationale note.
PASS = file contains a rationale covering loss ratio, rate change, exposure and deviations, with required approvals; FAIL = missing rationale element, no deviation justification, or missing approval.
Incomplete files are returned to the underwriter for completion within 5 business days; systemic documentation gaps are escalated to the Underwriting Director / Manager and captured in the QA log.
Field/element definitions from the renewal file-documentation standard (loss_ratio, rate_change, exposure_change, deviation_reason, approver) captured on the file template.
Control total = bound-renewal count reconciled to filed-rationale count with 0 delta, verified in the monthly QA review.

Approved methodology = renewal file-documentation standard v3; parameters (required rationale elements, sign-off thresholds) sourced from the underwriting quality standard and referenced in the file template header.
